PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026
description:
Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026 Procurement Summary Item Details RFP title Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Supplier type Research or data-collection agency Contract type Framework/on-call arrangement using task orders Geographic scope Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia and South Ethiopia Anticipated contract period October 2026 to September 2027 RFP issue date 5 October 2026 Proposal deadline 12 October 2026 Submission email suppliers@girleffect.org Proposal validity 90 days Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. Background Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young people's aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship. Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways. The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include: Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market. Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses. Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship. Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another. Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways. School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities. Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegna's established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young people's awareness and uptake of available opportunities. Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment. Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions. Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young people's knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes. The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions. The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programme's contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia. Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopia's tools, sample design, and quality standards. Who You Are The ideal candidate/Agency will: Have demonstrated experience managing field-based data collection for household, community, or individual-level surveys in Ethiopia, ideally on youth, gender, education, livelihoods, or social behaviour change topics. Maintain, or be able to rapidly build, a roster of vetted, experienced enumerators with local language coverage and cultural familiarity across some or all of the six Yegna Gize regions (Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia), including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Have hands-on experience with mobile data collection platforms, particularly SurveyCTO, and the ability to train enumerators on tool use ahead of each deployment. Demonstrate robust field supervision and data quality assurance practices — spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and real-time progress monitoring against a sample plan. Have in-house or readily available capacity for data cleaning, processing, and first-level quantitative and/or qualitative analysis, with clear documentation of methods. Be able to mobilize and scale data collection teams on short notice against a recurring, on-call task-order structure, without compromising quality or timeliness. Show a genuine commitment to Girl Effect's mission and values, with a demonstrated understanding of child/adolescent safeguarding standards appropriate to research involving youth. Be highly organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple concurrent task orders across different regions. What You will do 2.1 Geographic Coverage Data collection will take place across 6 regions and 60+ woredas, including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Exact woreda-level assignments will be shared with the selected agency alongside each task order, together with the corresponding sample size and tool set. 2.2 Sourcing, Vetting, and Onboarding of Data Collectors The agency is responsible for building and maintaining a roster of qualified, experienced data collectors who can be deployed against Girl Effect Ethiopia's task orders. This includes: Recruiting data collectors with relevant prior experience in household or community-level data collection, ideally on similar topics (e.g., health, gender, youth, social behavior change). Ensuring appropriate local language coverage and cultural familiarity for each assigned region/woreda, including pastoralist communities. Verifying qualifications, references, and prior fieldwork experience before onboarding. Maintaining a sufficient bench of vetted collectors to meet fluctuating task-order demand without delays. Ensuring the data collectors are given a functioning tab and are trained on the use of survey CTO. 2.3 Training The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering: Use of Girl Effect Ethiopia's data collection tools and mobile data collection platform. The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments. Data quality, ethics, consent, and child/adolescent safeguarding protocols appropriate to the population being surveyed. Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues. Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test). 2.4 Deployment Data collectors will be deployed per task order, which Girl Effect Ethiopia will issue for each data collection round/moment. Each task order will specify the woredas/regions, sample size, tools, timeline, and any round-specific instructions. The agency is responsible for: Assigning trained collectors to each task order based on location, language, and availability. Managing collector logistics (travel, accommodation, safety/security arrangements as applicable) within hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Providing day-to-day field supervision. 2.5 Data Quality and Timeliness The agency is accountable for the quality and timeliness of data collected under each task order, including: Real-time monitoring of data collection progress against the sample plan and timeline. Quality assurance mechanisms such as spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and review of flagged or inconsistent entries. Prompt escalation and resolution of fieldwork issues (e.g., inaccessible households, refusals, tool malfunctions) that could affect data quality or timelines. Regular progress reporting to Girl Effect Ethiopia (proposed: daily or weekly, to be agreed) showing completion rates by woreda/region. 2.6 Data Analysis and Submission Upon completion of each round of data collection, the agency will: Clean and process the collected data. Conduct analysis as specified in the task order. Submit the final clean dataset (in the agreed format), any cleaning/analysis syntax or code, and a summary report to Girl Effect Ethiopia within the timeline specified in the task order. Responsibilities The Hiring Organization and the selected Consultant/agency will have the following division of roles: Activity Girl Effect Ethiopia Contracted Agency Data collection tools & sampling frame Provides (already designed) Reviews & confirms understanding Data collector recruitment Sets qualification criteria; final sign-off Sources, screens candidates Training Provides technical/content input; approves training plan Organizes and delivers logistics Task orders Issues task order per round/moment Deploys collectors against task order Fieldwork supervision Spot-checks and technical backstopping Day-to-day field supervision Data quality assurance Defines quality standards; conducts audits Implements real-time QA checks Timeliness tracking Reviews progress dashboards Reports daily/weekly progress against timeline Data cleaning & analysis Reviews and validates Cleans, processes, and produces first-level analysis Submission Receives final dataset & report Submits clean dataset, syntax/code, and summary report Deliverables Specific deliverables for the duration of the engagement will include:- Roster of vetted, trained data collectors, updated and available on an ongoing basis. Training plan and completion records for each deployment. Field deployment plan per task order (collector-to-woreda assignment). Data collection progress reports (per agreed frequency) per task order. Quality assurance reports (back-check/spot-check findings and resolutions). Clean, validated datasets with accompanying documentation. First-level analysis and summary report per task order. Deliverables will be accepted when they meet the applicable task order, agreed quality standards and Girl Effect’s written feedback. The agency must correct substantiated quality issues attributable to its work at no additional fee. Expected Commitment This engagement is structured as a framework/on-call arrangement: the agency will be expected to mobilize data collectors on a per-task-order basis over the contract period between October 2026 and September 2027, with the frequency and scale of rounds varying according to program needs. Each task order will specify its own scope, sample, and timeline. Management The Consultant will have a primary point of contact within the Evidence & Insight team. Procurement Timeline Terms of Reference Published: Oct 5, 2026 Deadline for Proposal Submission: Oct 12, 2026 Proposal Submission Interested Consultant/agency should submit a maximum 10-page proposal that includes the following: Technical Proposal A CV or organizational profile outlining previous work and experience relevant to field data collection, enumerator training and management, and data analysis, particularly within the Ethiopian context and specifically highlighting experience across the Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, and/or South Ethiopia regions, including hard-to-reach or pastoralist areas where applicable. A brief overview of your understanding of Girl Effect's mission and the objectives of this assignment, and your proposed methodology — covering enumerator sourcing and vetting, training approach, field supervision structure, data quality assurance mechanisms (e.g., spot-checks, back-checks), and your approach to data cleaning and first-level analysis. Examples of at least two to three previous data collection and/or analysis assignments completed within the specified regions, demonstrating comparable scale, topic area, and quality outcomes. Reference — Provide at least three references for similar contracts with a description of the service provided, the value of the contract, and the contract periods of performance. Financial Proposal Please provide your proposed fee in ETB , including the total cost for impact the study assignment, along with a detailed breakdown by deliverable, aligned with the activities outlined in the Scope of Work for the region(s) you are applying to cover. Ensure that all applicable taxes are clearly itemized in your proposal. Evaluation Criteria Evaluation will follow three stages: Pre-screening Technical evaluation Financial evaluation Technical Evaluation – 70% No. Technical Evaluation Criterion Weight 1. Relevant Organizational Experience in Impact Evaluation, Research and Data Collection 15% 2. Understanding of Yegna Gize Programme and Assignment / TOR 10% 3. Proposed Research Methodology and Impact Evaluation Approach 20% 4. Sampling, Fieldwork and Data Collection Strategy 10% 5. Technical Capacity, Quality Assurance, Team Expertise and Operational Feasibility 15% Total Technical Score 70% Value for Money / Financial Competitiveness – 30% The financial scoring is based on the total evaluated cost , while also checking whether the proposed budget is sufficiently detailed and realistic across key cost categories such as personnel, training, fieldwork, travel/logistics, data management, analysis and reporting. GE is not liable for any cost incurred during the award/contract preparation, submission, or negotiation of the award/contract. All submitted documentation and/or materials shall become and remain the property of GE, and Technical & Financial proposals will need to be submitted as a separate document. Girl Effect may request clarifications, interviews, presentations, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers. The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected. General and Commercial Terms Framework and task orders: The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable framework agreement. Work may begin only after an authorised task order has been issued. The framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work. Contracting and Payment: The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones and receipt of a correct invoice. Girl Effect may withhold acceptance pending correction of material quality issues. Pricing, taxes and expenses: Prices must be quoted in Ethiopian Birr and remain firm during the proposal-validity period. Taxes and approved reimbursable expenses must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by Ethiopian law. Unapproved costs will not be reimbursed. Intellectual property and data ownership: Subject to the final agreement, Girl Effect will own the commissioned outputs, research data, instruments, documentation and analysis produced under the engagement. The agency may not reuse, publish or disclose these materials without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. Confidentiality and data protection: The agency must use personal and confidential information only for this assignment, apply appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, promptly report incidents and securely return or delete data when instructed. Safeguarding, ethics and conduct: The agency and all assigned personnel must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, informed-consent, ethical research, anti-fraud, information-security and supplier-conduct requirements. Required checks and training must be completed before deployment. Personnel and subcontracting: Changes to key personnel and the use of subcontractors require Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The agency will remain responsible for the quality, conduct and performance of all subcontracted work. Conflicts of interest: Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest. Equal opportunity: Girl Effect is committed to equal opportunity and encourages submissions from organisations with strong local knowledge and diverse professional and cultural backgrounds. Right to award: Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement, appoint more than one agency or make no award. Girl Effect will not reimburse proposal-preparation or negotiation costs. Proposal validity: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

How to Apply: ### **How To Apply** Email the technical and financial proposals as separate attachments to: **suppliers@girleffect.org.** Applications must be received by **12th October 2026.** Use the subject line: **Yegna Gize Field Research Services –Ethiopia** Submissions that do not follow the stated application process may not be evaluated. Only successful bidder or bidders will be notified.

title: 23257 Chief Migration Health Officer (P)

Responsibilities and Accountabilities Health Assessment Portfolio Organize and supervise the migration health assessment process to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries in the areas of: 1. Medical examinations 2. Imaging 3. Laboratory testing 4. Vaccinations 5. TB management 6. Treatment and referrals 7. Pre-departure procedures and medical movements 8. Documentation, certification and information transmission 9. title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Education Bachelor's degree required. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 05 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. title: Compliance and Systems Director for Ethiopia
description:
Contract Length: 1 year with the possibility of extension Country Programme : Ethiopia Base : Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Line Manager : Country Director for Ethiopia People in Need (PIN) is an international, non-profit organization providing humanitarian assistance and development cooperation worldwide. PIN adopts a triple nexus approach, linking humanitarian, development and resilience programming, with a strong focus on systems strengthening, locally led action and support to civil society. About the Ethiopia Programme of People in Need Present in Ethiopia since 2003, PIN works in partnership with communities, local organisations and public institutions to support sustainable development and improve people’s well-being across the country. Through integrated programming, PIN combines immediate assistance with longer-term, systems-oriented approaches aimed at strengthening resilience, expanding access to essential services and economic opportunities, and enabling locally led solutions. Guided by its Relief and Development strategy, PIN operates across multiple regions and works with a diverse portfolio of institutional donors and partners. About the role: The Compliance and Systems Director (CSD) is a member of the country programme senior management (together with the Country Director (CD) and Head of Programmes (HoP)/Program Manager (ProgM)) and shares responsibility for the effective and efficient delivery of People in Need’s (PIN) country programme. Specifically, CSD leads and oversees organisational compliance by providing guidance to staff on the application and enforcement of internal and external regulations. This includes ensuring the interpretation and implementation of donors’ contractual requirements and adherence to PIN internal procedures. The role of the CSD is to manage and improve the support systems and operations required to achieve this objective comprising of Logistic, Procurement, Finance and HR agendas. In performing this role, the CSD also ensures an enabling environment for the implementation of the country programme, while maintaining operations and systems that meet with the accountability requirements of PIN and its donors. CSD also directly leads the process of the development and staff capacity building across the departments. Reporting Relations & Interdependencies with Other Functions The CSD´s line manager is CD. Technically the CSD is supervised by the Regional Head of Systems and Operations based at HQ. At country programme level, the CSD is the line manager of the Head of Finance, Head of Operations, HR Manager, or, should this position be unfilled, to another equivalent supervisory role. The CSD also works closely with DCD-P and Programme and Project Managers. description:
PLEASE NOTE: This search is being conducted by Ethiojobs. Please apply DIRECTLY through the link below : https://ethiojobs.net/job/UAVcbgg81M-government-relations-advisor-africa-vital-strategies _________________ Vital Strategies is an international public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury and death. We currently work in 73 countries, supporting data-driven decision making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include non-communicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, obesity prevention, overdose prevention, environmental health, and vital statistics systems building. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. The candidate must have authorization to work legally in the respective country at the time of hire. Vital Strategies offers highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position will vary by location, experience and qualifications. Duties and Responsibilities: Regional program coordination and strategic vision - · In coordination with the global team, facilitate regional exchanges and development of regional partnerships and a consistent strategy for government engagement and partnership building in the region; · Initiate and/or sustain government partnerships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and other national and regional institutions in priority countries; · Support project launches and startups in new countries within the region, including support for staff recruitment; · Support country teams in translating strategy into implementation plans, including identification of key capacity gaps to be filled, and government engagement needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of program activities; · Identify and participate in regional opportunities and events that help elevate lead poisoning on national agendas; · Promote multisectoral collaboration and partnership-driven approaches to environmental health policy development; · Manage relationships with regional organizations engaged in lead-related activities, and develop, where appropriate, formal or contractual relationships for discrete programmatic activities in support of the initiative. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Qualifications: Education & Degree - · Master’s degree in public health, public policy/Administration, Global Health, international development, environmental health science, or related field. Skills & Abilities - · Strong government engagement and partnership-building skills, with the ability to establish and sustain relationships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and regional institutions; · Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-country initiatives and facilitate regional exchange and collaboration; · Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate regional strategy into actionable country-level implementation plans; · Strong stakeholder management skills across government, NGOs, multilateral agencies, and technical partners; · Ability to promote and facilitate multisectoral collaboration and policy dialogue; · Ability to monitor program quality, performance, and outcomes across a regional portfolio; · Ability to coordinate and engage program stakeholders and other country teams; · Demonstrated sensitivity in handling confidential information; · Proven ability to interpret public health data, generate actionable insights, and support policy recommendations; · Exhibits strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines; demonstrates personal integrity, credibility, and professionalism while taking initiative and making sound, informed decisions in a fast-paced environment; · Professional oral and written proficiency in English; · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to an interdisciplinary international team; · Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook); · Experience working with a geographically distributed team with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, communicate clearly and regularly, monitor performance, and inspire, engage, and motivate staff; · Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment. Experience: Required - · Minimum of eight years of experience in government engagement and public health programming, ideally with experience in health policy, environmental health, and/or global health, especially related to lead poisoning prevention or environmental pollution; · Experience in representing organizations with governments, international institutions, and senior stakeholder forums; · Experience managing multi-country programs in Africa; · Experience working with government agencies, regulatory bodies, and public health facilities; · Experience with program reporting and monitoring. Preferred - · Demonstrated experience in communicating scientific and health information to varied audiences; · Experience in using project management platforms. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: · If hired in Ghana, Rwanda, or Tanzania, the candidate will be hired via Vital Strategies’ Employer of Record on a remote schedule; · The position will require travel up to 30% of the time to visit operating countries in the region to visit field implementation or attend meetings with partners; · The candidate needs to be willing to work with colleagues across different time zones.

title: Technical Field Manager - HMA
description:
The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

POSITION PROFILE

The National HMA Technical Field Manager (TFM) is responsible for supporting the Operations Manager (OM) in the overall planning, implementation, quality control, and monitoring of all MA activities in country. The TFM provides continuous technical advice to teams under his/her responsibility in order to develop the capacity and technical knowledge of national mine action staff to ensure correct and safe implementation of activities according to IMAS, Sudan NMAS and standard operating procedures (SOPs), and so that sustainable technical capacity is developed within the country programme. The TFM is the liaison between the local partner and the OM.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities: (in bullet points)


	
		
			
			Staff management & supervision:

			
				Support the local partner’s planning and recruitment of teams as per project requirements
				Design and deliver training for survey and clearance staff and oversee accreditation of teams, design and deliver training to partners as required
				Conduct periodic refresher training for survey and clearance staff and ensure the skills of teams are according to applicable internal and international standards
				Mentor, manage, monitor and supervise the teams under your responsibility, ensuring that they carry out their duties safely and in accordance with SOPs and ensure that implementation is consistent with the national partner SOP, IMAS international standards, and Sudan NMAS and ensure that implementation is consistent with the partner SOP and DRC SOP (when applicable), IMAS international standards, and Sudan NMAS
				Ensure that teams have the necessary materials and other equipment to carry out the designated activities
				Support with the planning and delivery of MA trainings to ensure capacity building of the HMA sector in Sudan
			

			Planning, monitoring & quality management:

title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study
description:
Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. 

That’s the Girl Effect.

Background

Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young peoples aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship.

Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways.

The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young peoples knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.

Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include:

  • Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market.
  • Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses.
  • Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship.
  • Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another.
  • Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways.
  • School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities.
  • Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegnas established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young peoples awareness and uptake of available opportunities.
  • Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment.

Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions.

Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study

As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young peoples knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes.

The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions.

The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programmes contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia.

Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopias tools, sample design, and quality standards.

  • Maintain, or be able to rapidly build, a roster of vetted, experienced enumerators with local language coverage and cultural familiarity across some or all of the six Yegna Gize regions (Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia), including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas.

  • Ensuring the data collectors are given a functioning tab and are trained on the use of survey CTO.

The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering:

  • Use of Girl Effect Ethiopias data collection tools and mobile data collection platform.
  • The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments.
  • Data quality, ethics, consent, and child/adolescent safeguarding protocols appropriate to the population being surveyed.
  • Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues.

Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test).

  • Providing day-to-day field supervision.

The agency is accountable for the quality and timeliness of data collected under each task order, including:

  • Real-time monitoring of data collection progress against the sample plan and timeline.
  • Quality assurance mechanisms such as spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and review of flagged or inconsistent entries.
  • Prompt escalation and resolution of fieldwork issues (e.g., inaccessible households, refusals, tool malfunctions) that could affect data quality or timelines.
  • Regular progress reporting to Girl Effect Ethiopia (proposed: daily or weekly, to be agreed) showing completion rates by woreda/region.

title: Ethiopia Innovations and Growth Lead
description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.
